feedback: Accepted. Format: header is complete (STATES declares u0-u4, INITIAL_STATE u0, nonempty FINAL_STATES: u4 which is declared and is the accepting state reached exactly on target_picked_up); transition/reward syntax matches the paper format and every reward triple corresponds to a listed transition; every state has an else self-loop, so irrelevant or out-of-window events (door_open and target_picked_up before they are possible, has_door_key alone in u0/u1, blocker_moved fluctuations in u3/u4) are absorbed. Semantic fidelity: the 5-state chain u0 (start) -> u1 (blocker moved) -> u2 (matching key held while blocker still away) -> u3 (door open) -> u4 (target box picked up) encodes the task's ordering 'move the ball away before taking the key' as a soft preference: the key-first strategy is physically possible, but it never progresses in u0 and the forced drop (hands must free up for the ball) fires key_lost at -0.3, so ball-first is strictly preferred (1.6 vs 1.3 total). The u1->u2 guard 'has_door_key & blocker_moved' correctly re-checks the non-latching blocker_moved at key-pickup time, handling the case where the ball was dropped back on the door cell; no has_ball-style carrying latch is assumed, matching the blocker_moved condition reading. Persistent/event distinctions are handled right: key_lost is used as a one-step event trigger, and dropping the key after the door is open correctly does NOT fire key_lost (u3 else-loop), matching the example trace's step-19 drop. Regressions are explicit where required: (u2, key_lost) -> u1 sends the agent back to re-acquire the key; u0/u1 key_lost self-loops prevent re-rewarding earlier milestones (re-picking the ball in u1 yields no duplicate +0.1). Reward safety: milestone rewards +0.1/+0.2/+0.3/+1.0 are dense across the chain, each paid once, bounded; every cycle back is net-negative (u2<->u1 drop/re-pick costs -0.1; u0 key-first costs -0.3), so there is no reward farming; u4 is absorbing with zero reward. Reachability: u4 is reachable from every state with no dead ends (a u1 agent holding the key with the ball back in front escapes via the key_lost drop, then re-does ball then key). Minor non-blocking notes: the u0 key-first attempt is penalized at the forced drop rather than at the pickup itself (unavoidable with proposition-only events, since has_door_key alone in u0 is also the benign pre-key state of the good trajectory), and repeated key drops can accumulate negative reward, but every such cycle is self-punishing rather than exploitable. No rewrite needed.

All five declared propositions are present, no undeclared extras, and each aligns with the documented truth conditions. blocker_moved: the scan-by-type finds the single door and checks the cell at (dx-1, dy) (the documented ball cell) for a ball; the `x > 0` guard short-circuits before any out-of-range grid.get call, and since the layout guarantees the ball cell is the door's left neighbor with dx >= 1, this is equivalent to the reference expression — it turns true when the ball is picked up (cell empty/ball in hand), turns false again if the ball is dropped back on that cell, and stays true if the ball is dropped elsewhere or the cell holds a non-ball object. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up are verbatim equivalents of the reference expressions (carrying-key-with-matching-door-color, any open door, carrying box matching the mission string). key_lost is a correct event: it reads prev['has_door_key'] from the read-only previous_valuation snapshot, recomputes not-K and not-D from current state (correct event semantics rather than a lingering reading), is false on the first step (short-circuits safely if the snapshot is absent/None), and is false whenever prev lacks has_door_key, the key is carried, or the door is open — satisfying the stated mutual exclusions with has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up. The code is syntactically valid, imports nothing, performs no actions, and mutates neither the environment nor episode_memory.
